name: Chuck Schumer

note: Candidate.

note: Alsobrooks's office declined to clarify the position on Nov 16-17 before the Nov 18 declaration.

name: Tammy Baldwin
stance_summary: Official statement of support for Schumer.
note: Link taken from the whip tracker; not yet opened.

name: Richard Blumenthal
stance_summary: Said on Nov 9 that Blumenthal plans to support Schumer as majority leader, after calling for new energy in the caucus.

name: Sherrod Brown
stance_summary: Incoming senator; says Schumer knows how to govern.

name: John Fetterman
stance_summary: Backs Schumer; called a Van Hollen win troubling (Fox News interview).

name: Ruben Gallego
stance_summary: "When the manager takes you to the World Series, you give him another contract."

name: Kirsten Gillibrand
stance_summary: Praised Schumer's strategic leadership; backs Schumer.

name: Mazie Hirono
stance_summary: "I'm supporting Chuck because of the long history I have with Chuck."

note: Link taken from the whip tracker; not yet opened. Quote from The Hill via our dataset.

name: Catherine Cortez Masto
stance_summary: Posted on X that Schumer was instrumental in the majority and "I will be supporting him as our Democratic leader."
note: X posts can't be read by our checker.

name: Jack Reed
stance_summary: Official statement of support for Schumer.

name: Jacky Rosen
stance_summary: Said Schumer "has the experience and the fight to continue leading our diverse caucus."
note: X posts can't be read by our checker.

name: Brian Schatz
stance_summary: Publicly supports Schumer; expected to be the next whip.
note: Secondhand: a news outlet's list. The tracker links a Punchbowl article whose URL slug is about Thune, so it was not used.

name: Mark Warner
stance_summary: Reported to have endorsed Schumer on Nov 25; earlier uncommitted (Nov 10-11).
note: DISPUTED/NEW: the tracker (last checked Nov 20) lists Warner undecided. The Washington Post (Nov 25) and Wikipedia list Warner for Schumer, after an earlier no-commitment on Nov 24.

name: Sheldon Whitehouse
stance_summary: Reported backing Schumer, alongside Jack Reed.
note: The earlier Washington Post link did not name Whitehouse when checked, so it was replaced.

name: Chris Van Hollen
stance_summary: Announced on Nov 12 a challenge to Schumer; claims support from more than 15 senators, though only a few have said so publicly.
note: Candidate.

name: Jeff Merkley
stance_summary: Endorsed Van Hollen on X.
note: Link taken from the whip tracker; not yet opened.

name: Bernie Sanders
stance_summary: Won't back Schumer; endorsed Van Hollen: "the time is now for change."

name: Elissa Slotkin
stance_summary: "Because I've been clear that I wasn't supporting Schumer, I will be supporting Chris Van Hollen."
note: Endorsed in a video on Nov 19. The tracker's own link for Slotkin points to an unrelated article, so it was not used.

name: Abdul El-Sayed
stance_summary: First senator-elect to back Van Hollen; introduced Van Hollen as the next majority leader.
note: Secondhand: a news outlet's list of Van Hollen's backers.

name: Peggy Flanagan
stance_summary: Backs Van Hollen; called for new leadership in the Senate.
note: Secondhand: a news outlet's list of Van Hollen's backers.

name: Troy Jackson
stance_summary: Endorsed Van Hollen on Nov 25; before that, opposed Schumer without naming a pick.
note: DISPUTED/RESOLVED: the tracker (last checked Nov 20) shows Jackson with no pick and links a Nov 9 article. Newer reports (WGME, Washington Post, Press Herald, Washington Examiner) confirm the Nov 25 endorsement.

name: Adam Hamilton
stance_summary: Won't support Schumer; has not backed Van Hollen.

name: Michael Bennet
stance_summary: Has not committed; says the caucus needs a serious debate.

name: Cory Booker
stance_summary: Wants a family conversation within the caucus; hasn't committed.

name: Maria Cantwell
stance_summary: Credited Schumer for the win but will listen to the debate first.
note: Oldest statement in this group (Nov 4).

name: Chris Coons
stance_summary: Open to hearing other candidates; has called Van Hollen's chances remote.

name: Martin Heinrich
stance_summary: Not saying whom to back; wants to hear from the incoming freshmen first.

name: John Hickenlooper
stance_summary: Won't commit to Schumer; says it's healthy to review how the caucus works.

name: Tim Kaine
stance_summary: Defended Schumer after the win but is open to Van Hollen or another candidate, per AP.
note: DISPUTED: the tracker lists Kaine as leaning toward Schumer; Wikipedia and the AP wording support uncommitted.

name: Andy Kim
stance_summary: Uncommitted; wants a caucus discussion first.

name: Ed Markey
stance_summary: Declined to endorse Schumer; office says it is open to new leadership.

name: Chris Murphy
stance_summary: Avoided committing when asked in March; a Nov 20 report counts Murphy among senators who remain uncommitted.

name: Patty Murray
stance_summary: Didn't commit either way; says the caucus will decide.

name: Jon Ossoff
stance_summary: Has not committed to either; wants to hear each candidate's vision.

name: Alex Padilla
stance_summary: Noncommittal before a caucus lunch.

name: Raphael Warnock
stance_summary: Won't commit; says Democrats are at an inflection point.

name: Elizabeth Warren
stance_summary: Has not publicly said whom to back.
note: The tracker's own link for Warren is an October article, so it was replaced.

name: Peter Welch
stance_summary: Reported undecided after earlier being seen as a Schumer backer; a spokesperson says Welch is discussing the race.

name: Ron Wyden
stance_summary: Wouldn't say whether Wyden supports any leadership changes, including for Schumer.

name: Ben Ray Luján
stance_summary: Won't say who gets the vote; wants commitments from both candidates.
note: Wikipedia lists Luján as 'unknown support'; Roll Call reports a refusal to say.

name: Annie Andrews
stance_summary: Said on Nov 17 that no candidate has been picked yet and talks with both are ongoing; has called for "generational change."
note: DISPUTED/RESOLVED: the tracker lists Andrews opposed to Schumer, based on a Nov 15 report. The later Nov 17 Post and Courier piece says undecided. A Washington Examiner report later that week says Andrews still appears to oppose Schumer keeping the role.

name: Scott Colom
stance_summary: Still listening; doesn't know either candidate well, per CNN.

name: Chris Pappas
stance_summary: Called for a new generation of leadership but has not said whom to back.
note: The tracker's CNN live-blog link was replaced by this NHPR report.

name: Juliana Stratton
stance_summary: Said on Nov 12 that Stratton continues to oppose Schumer; an NBC segment on Nov 18 is headlined as undecided and hearing everybody out.
note: DISPUTED: the tracker lists Stratton leaning against Schumer, which fits. Wikipedia lists Stratton uncommitted. Stratton opposes Schumer but has not named a pick.

name: James Talarico
stance_summary: Hasn't taken sides yet.

name: Josh Turek
stance_summary: Has met both candidates and wants more specifics before deciding.

name: Lisa Blunt Rochester
stance_summary: No public statement on the race found.

name: Tammy Duckworth
stance_summary: No public statement on the race found.

name: Maggie Hassan
stance_summary: Reported as mum on the choice.

name: Adam Schiff
stance_summary: No public statement on the race found.
note: Trackers conflict: one lists Schiff leaning Schumer (Semafor, Nov 10), another lists no statement found. No direct statement found.

name: Roy Cooper
stance_summary: Campaign statement dodged a question about Schumer; an ally of Schumer says Cooper's vote is locked, which Cooper has not confirmed.

name: Mary Peltola
stance_summary: Has not taken sides yet; the race was called Nov 17.
